issues.title: Traditional namespace declaration with braces
issues.description: The rule requires C# files to use file-scoped namespace declarations (ending with semicolon without braces), but this file uses traditional namespace declarations with opening and closing braces.

issues.title: Incorrect type conversion in generic component parameter assertion
issues.description: The test validates a generic component with an int type parameter but uses Convert.ToInt64 instead of Convert.ToInt32 to assert the parameter value. Since the parameter is defined as int (System.Int32) in GenericTestComponent<int>, this creates a type mismatch. The assertion compares a long (Int64) value to the expected int (Int32) value 42, which will cause the test to fail even though the component deserialization is working correctly. This breaks the validation logic for generic component parameters.

issues.title: Incorrect sequence validation for multiple generic components
issues.description: The test validates deserialization of multiple closed generic components but checks that both descriptors have sequence number 0 instead of verifying that the second descriptor has sequence number 1. Component descriptors in a collection must have sequential ordering starting from 0, and this test should verify the second component has sequence 1. This incorrect assertion fails to validate proper sequence ordering, which is critical for component initialization and rendering order in Blazor.

issues.title: Generic type parameter mismatch in component marker validation
issues.description: The test creates and renders a GenericComponent<int> with value 456, but then validates the component marker against GenericComponent<string> type instead of GenericComponent<int>. This causes the test to check for the wrong fully qualified type name and assembly metadata. The type validation will fail because the actual rendered component is GenericComponent<int> while the test expects GenericComponent<string>, breaking the validation of WebAssembly component prerendering for closed generic types.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64643 - Add test coverage for prerendering closed generic components

structured_output.summary:
This PR is tests only. It adds a `GenericComponent<TValue>` Razor test component and four `EndpointHtmlRendererTest` cases covering static, server (prerendered and not) and WebAssembly prerendering of closed generic components. It also adds four `ServerComponentDeserializerTest` cases that round-trip closed generic types through the server descriptor protocol. The goal is to show that `Type.FullName` plus `Assembly.GetType` already handle closed generics, so no product change is needed.

The idea is sound and the server-mode renderer tests are careful. But two of the new tests will fail as written. `CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ClientMode` renders `GenericComponent<int>` and then asserts the marker's `TypeName` against `GenericComponent<string>`. `CanParseMultipleMarkersForClosedGenericComponents` expects the second descriptor's `Sequence` to be 0, but `CreateMarkers` assigns 0, 1, and the deserializer requires sequences to increase. The PR also rewrites the deserializer test file from a file-scoped namespace to a block-scoped one without re-indenting, which adds noise and breaks the repo's conventions.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two of the new tests have wrong assertions (wrong generic argument, wrong sequence number) and will fail in CI. Since the PR's whole point is to show the feature works, its tests need to pass. The namespace rewrite should also be reverted.

architecture.overview:
On the server, `EndpointHtmlRenderer.PrerenderComponentAsync` renders a root component and, for interactive render modes, writes HTML comment markers that describe the component. For Interactive Server, `ServerComponentSerializer` records `AssemblyName` and `TypeName` (from `type.FullName`) plus the parameters in a data-protected descriptor. For WebAssembly, `WebAssemblyComponentSerializer` writes the assembly name and `FullName` into the marker in plain text. When a circuit starts, `ServerComponentDeserializer` unprotects the descriptors, checks that sequence numbers run 0..n and share one invocation ID, and resolves the type with `GetRootType(assembly, typeName)`.

The PR leaves all of this unchanged. It adds tests showing that a closed generic `FullName` (with assembly-qualified type arguments) survives the trip through these serializers and resolves back to the same type.
steps: `EndpointHtmlRenderer.PrerenderComponentAsync` is the entry point. The new tests call it with `typeof(GenericComponent<int>)` / `GenericComponent<string>` and the null, InteractiveServer and InteractiveWebAssembly render modes.
For server mode, `ServerComponentSerializer` writes a protected descriptor holding `TypeName = type.FullName`. The new tests unprotect it and compare it to the closed generic's `FullName`.
For WebAssembly mode, `WebAssemblyComponentSerializer.SerializeInvocation` puts `type.FullName` straight into the marker. The new client-mode test reads `preambleMarker.TypeName`.

On reconnect, `ServerComponentDeserializer.TryDeserializeComponentDescriptorCollection` checks sequence ordering and invocation IDs, then resolves the type. The new deserializer tests round-trip `GenericTestComponent<T>` markers through it.
Test fixtures: `TestComponents/GenericComponent.razor` (`@typeparam TValue`) and a private nested `GenericTestComponent<T>` in the deserializer test.

findings.title: Client-mode test checks the marker against GenericComponent<string> but renders GenericComponent<int>
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Endpoints/test/EndpointHtmlRendererTest.cs`, the test `CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ClientMode` (around lines 817-846) prerenders `GenericComponent<int>` but asserts `preambleMarker.Assembly` and `preambleMarker.TypeName` against `typeof(GenericComponent<string>)`. Change both assertions (around lines 837-838) to use `typeof(GenericComponent<int>)` so they match the rendered type. Optionally, also check the marker's parameter definitions/values, following the pattern in `CanPrerender_ComponentWithParameters_ClientMode`.

findings.title: Multi-marker generic test expects the second descriptor's Sequence to be 0
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Server/test/Circuits/ServerComponentDeserializerTest.cs`, the test `CanParseMultipleMarkersForClosedGenericComponents` (around lines 128-146) asserts `Assert.Equal(0, secondDescriptor.Sequence)`. The second marker produced by `CreateMarkers` has sequence 1, and the deserializer requires sequences to increase by one, so change the expected value to 1. This matches the existing `CanParseMultipleMarkers` test.

findings.title: File-scoped namespace converted to a block namespace without re-indenting
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Server/test/Circuits/ServerComponentDeserializerTest.cs`, revert the namespace change at lines 10-13: restore the file-scoped `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits;` followed by `public class ServerComponentDeserializerTest` and `{`, and delete the extra trailing `}` at the end of the file. Keep the new `using System.Globalization;`, the new test methods and the `GenericTestComponent<T>` class.

findings.title: Only framework types are tested as generic arguments
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Server/test/Circuits/ServerComponentDeserializerTest.cs`, add a test like `CanParseSingleMarkerForClosedGenericComponentWithUserTypeArgument` that serializes and deserializes `GenericTestComponent<TestComponent>` (a non-BCL type argument). Assert that `descriptor.ComponentType` equals `typeof(GenericTestComponent<TestComponent>)`. Follow the existing `CanParseSingleMarkerForClosedGenericComponent` test (around lines 79-91). If possible, also add a case whose type argument comes from a different assembly than the component.

findings.title: Server-mode renderer tests check the protected descriptor closely
findings.body: `CanRender_ClosedGenericComponent_ServerMode` and `CanPrerender_ClosedGenericComponent_ServerMode` unprotect the descriptor and check `TypeName` against the closed generic's `FullName`, the parameter definition (`System.String` from `System.Private.CoreLib`), the parameter value and the preamble/epilogue `PrerenderId` pairing. They follow the existing `GreetingComponent` tests closely, so they're easy to read next to their neighbors.
